walkthroughs.body_html:
Materials — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Materials brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Materials.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A wire of length 2.0 m and area 1.0 mm² extends by 1.0 mm under 100 N. Young's modulus is:
options: 2.0 × 10¹¹ Pa
1.0 × 10¹¹ Pa
Force per unit area
Extension per unit length
Stress per unit volume
Stress × Young's modulus
The stiffness of a material — the ratio of stress to strain in the elastic region.
Young's modulus measures how strong a material is — how much force it can take before breaking.
Young's modulus measures the density of a material.
It becomes more elastic and can stretch further.

mcqs.q: What is the formula for Young's modulus?
options: It becomes more elastic and can stretch further.
Extension / original length — the same as strain.
Stress / strain — the ratio in the linear (elastic) region of a stress-strain graph.
Force / area — the same as stress itself.

mcqs.q: What happens to a metal wire stretched beyond its elastic limit?
options: It becomes more elastic and can stretch further.
It snaps immediately at the elastic limit.
It deforms plastically and will not return to its original length when the load is removed.
Extension / original length — the same as strain.
